races.name: Book Your Christmas Party Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Holy Joe
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's six-year-old has a recent win on Good ground and a prominent style that sits perfectly behind Dolly Dior here; 37 days since last run is not a concern for this stable and the step back in trip from his last run actually suits his form profile.

runners_data.name: L'amalric
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy's five-year-old has solid Good-ground novice form (3/3 in similar going) and is a natural front-runner by inclination, though in this field with Dolly Dior taking the lead he is likely to race closer to midfield than his preferred position; Sean Bowen is a major booking but the positional compromise is real.

runners_data.name: Dolly Dior
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter in this race, Dolly Dior has a win on Good ground over 2m and jumps with enough confidence to control a small field; Patrick Neville's runners are out of form in the last 14 days (0/6) which is a mild flag, and the OR of 120 in a novice suggests she must carry her rating well.

runners_data.name: Moi Mon Vieux
runners_data.note: A lightly-raced four-year-old with only four career runs and an undefined running style, the tongue-tie is noted and he steps up in trip having won on Good ground; Richard Hobson has no current yard momentum (0/0 in 14 days) and the thin form sample makes him genuinely hard to assess.

runners_data.name: Fortunes Dawn
runners_data.note: William Young Jnr's seven-year-old is a hold-up type whose last two runs on similar going both resulted in no-show finishes (7th and 9th); Derek Fox takes over in the saddle but Fortunes Dawn needs a pace scenario that is simply unlikely to materialise here.

races.paceDynamic: Dolly Dior is the confirmed front-runner here and, facing just four rivals in a 2m4f novice hurdle on Good ground at Perth, she should be able to dictate an unchallenged, controlled tempo from the front. Holy Joe and L'amalric are both natural prominent racers, but with Dolly Dior taking the lead role, they will be shuffled into a chasing pack rather than sharing the front; L'amalric in particular is mapped to midfield because the field holds more genuinely prominent types than can all secure that position, meaning Holy Joe is best-placed to claim the second slot. The likely result is a single-file, measured pace that keeps the race honest without stringing it out — Good ground over 2m4f at Perth tends to reward those who travel economically and jump fluently, not those who need a true test of stamina. This race shape strongly favours a well-placed prominent racer who can track Dolly Dior throughout and pounce over the final two flights, with pure hold-up horses like Fortunes Dawn at a disadvantage against a pace that may not be hot enough to bring them into it late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dolly Dior Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Dolly Dior jumps cleanly from the gate and establishes an uncontested lead at a sustainable gallop.
scenarios.body: Dolly Dior dictates from the front, setting a rhythm that suits her jumping style and denies rivals the opportunity to build momentum off a true pace; the prominent trackers Holy Joe and L'amalric are the main dangers if they travel well enough to mount a final-flight challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Dolly Dior's pace is just hot enough over the final circuit to leave her vulnerable, and Holy Joe or L'amalric travels smoothly to challenge.
scenarios.body: Holy Joe, with Sean Bowen in the saddle for L'amalric and Rian Corcoran on Holy Joe, are both primed to travel in the slipstream and strike from the penultimate hurdle; the Gordon Elliott/Holy Joe combination carries obvious class in this novice company.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Moi Mon Vieux Improves Late
scenarios.trigger: If the lightly-raced four-year-old Moi Mon Vieux handles the step up in trip and Good ground to produce an improved display.
scenarios.body: Moi Mon Vieux is an unknown quantity with only four career runs and an unknown style profile, but the step to 2m4f on Good ground could unlock improvement; the downside is the thin form record and a trainer posting 0/0 in the last 14 days offers no momentum.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce in Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace completely collapses in the home straight and Fortunes Dawn, a genuine hold-up horse, gets a strong late run.
scenarios.body: Fortunes Dawn has not shown the ability to win off these marks (0W0P in the last two similar-going runs) and needs a stronger pace than Dolly Dior is likely to set to get competitive; this scenario is the least probable given the moderate tempo expected.

watchPoints.text: Watch Dolly Dior at the first hurdle — if she gets in a tangle or is slow to jump, Holy Joe could inherit the lead and the entire race map changes.
L'amalric is a natural front-runner but will be boxed behind Dolly Dior; watch for Sean Bowen attempting to push forward early, which could inject unexpected pressure into the race in the first mile.
Moi Mon Vieux wears a tongue-tie and is unproven at 2m4f — watch whether he travels fluently on the first circuit or gets outpaced as the field settles.

Fortunes Dawn has shown no ability to win off these marks in two recent Good-ground starts; watch whether Derek Fox elects to hunt round quietly or makes an uncharacteristic move from off the pace, which would signal a significant market move was warranted.

races.name: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Ras Kassar
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with solid recent form (11-101) over Irish hurdles, but steps up in trip on turf for French trainer Boisnard — the class and style combination could suit if pace is genuine, though 42 days off and an apprentice rider on a horse with a hurdles-heavy profile add uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Ras Kassar remains unexposed and open to improvement, with four wins in his last five starts underlining plenty of ability. An unplaced effort two starts back is the only blip in an otherwise ultra-consistent sequence. He returns after a 42-day break carrying 167 lb, with more clearly still to come.

runners_data.name: Conquer The Breeze
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a strong record at 16f on Good (2W from recent similar-going runs), Ryan Mania gives a significant experience advantage, and a T14 strike rate of 1/5 for Adam Nicol keeps the stable angle modest but relevant — the key runner in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Conquer The Breeze is an outsider on our figures despite three wins in his last five starts, including his latest outing — the pulled-up effort right at the start of that sequence is the concern behind the modest placing. He has proven form over today's trip and going, back within 21 days.

runners_data.name: Hypotenus
runners_data.note: Placed consistently at 16f on Good and similar ground (4/16f/GOO, 3/16f/SOF) and likely to sit midfield under Richie McLernon; Neil Mulholland's runner has solid place claims at this trip but has not won in recent starts, suggesting a place rather than a win profile.
runners_data.comment: Hypotenus is the one to beat on these figures on the strength of admirable consistency — three thirds in his last five starts, even without a win in that time. He has proven form over today's trip and going, though a sixth earlier in the sequence and 35 days off are considerations.

runners_data.name: Tree Top Tyson
runners_data.note: Returned after 171 days off which is the standout concern here — Brian Hughes is a quality booking but this horse has a prominent style that will need fitness to be spot-on; the 2m trip and Good going suit on past form, but the layoff makes his chance conditional.
runners_data.comment: Tree Top Tyson is a leading danger, a winner four starts back, and runner-up five starts back, with a fourth three starts back too. He has proven form over today's trip and going, though his last two starts - fifth and pulled up - plus a 171-day absence are the concerns.

runners_data.name: Garde Des Champs
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old with consistent placed form on Good ground (3/20f, 3/16f recently), but his natural running style is hold-up, not midfield — he's been placed in the map ahead of his true position because the field is back-heavy, and the controlled pace this race is likely to produce does not play to his strengths.
runners_data.comment: Garde Des Champs is a leading danger, winless in his last five starts but with back-to-back thirds in his latest two runs. Two fourths and an eighth make up the rest of that sequence. He has proven form over today's trip and going, and returns quickly within just 10 days.

runners_data.name: Kinbara Firstdraft
runners_data.note: Modest form figures (74-574) and a true hold-up horse placed artificially forward in the map due to the field's shape — Conor Rabbitt's 3lb claim barely offsets the reality that this horse needs a strong pace to challenge and is rated the lowest in the field at OR 100.
runners_data.comment: Kinbara Firstdraft is a leading danger on our figures despite being winless in his last five starts — a pair of fourths and two sevenths show a fairly modest scoreline, though a fifth in between adds some substance. He has proven form over today's trip and going, back within just 10 days.

races.paceDynamic: Conquer The Breeze is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner 2m chase and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, Ryan Mania can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front. Tree Top Tyson may try to press from a prominent position, but with Brian Hughes in the saddle on a horse returning after 171 days off, aggressive pace-forcing is unlikely. The remainder of the field — Ras Kassar, Hypotenus, Garde Des Champs, and Kinbara Firstdraft — are all hold-up or midfield types who will be chasing from off the pace, meaning Conquer The Breeze controls the tempo entirely. This race shape heavily favours the front-runner and any horse with a prominent style that can latch onto a single measured pace and pick up in the straight; pure hold-up horses will need the pace to be genuinely searching, which is not guaranteed here. Note that this field holds more hold-up types than the map can physically place at the rear — Garde Des Champs and Kinbara Firstdraft are true hold-up horses who have been redistributed to midfield, meaning they are unlikely to get the strong gallop their style demands.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Breeze Controls And Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Conquer The Breeze is allowed to dictate an uncontested lead throughout and the tempo stays measured.
scenarios.body: Mania sets an honest but controlled pace over 2m on Good ground, building a rhythm the hold-up horses cannot disrupt; the absence of any genuine pace rival means the front-runner's stamina and jumping fluency become decisive advantages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Conquer The Breeze sets enough pace to tire in the final half-mile and a pressing rival sweeps past.
scenarios.body: Tree Top Tyson, if fit after 171 days, could slot in just off the leader and use a prominent run to pounce if the pace bites; this scenario requires the front-runner to have set a stronger-than-expected tempo that drains its reserves.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the field strings out, leaving real ground to make up the home straight.
scenarios.body: Ras Kassar has the form to close from off the pace and the apprentice claim of Rian Corcoran (5) could prove a small tactical advantage in a race with a set pace; however, Garde Des Champs and Kinbara Firstdraft are not in their natural positions and their chances in this shape are materially discounted.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos Scrambles Order
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or a false pace causes the field to concertina, scrambling the anticipated running order.
scenarios.body: A small six-runner field on Good ground at Perth can occasionally see the pace collapse or a leader make a significant error, throwing the race open to any survivor; Hypotenus, who has been consistently placed on similar going, could benefit from any mid-race disruption.

watchPoints.text: Conquer The Breeze's jumping accuracy is critical — any unforced error at a fence could let Tree Top Tyson or a hold-up chaser use the mistake to close immediately in a small six-runner field.

Tree Top Tyson's fitness after 171 days off should be monitored in the paddock and at the start — if he shows any signs of ring-rustiness early, his ability to hold a prominent position and challenge in the straight will be significantly reduced.

Garde Des Champs and Kinbara Firstdraft are both true hold-up horses unable to get their natural position in this race shape — if the pace is slower than expected, they are effectively racing without their chief tactical weapon.

Ras Kassar has all his recent form over hurdles in Ireland (on Heavyish ground) and this switch to a chase on Good turf at Perth represents a notable change in context — watch for any early signs of unsettlement or jumping hesitation.

Alan Doyle's 3lb claim on Garde Des Champs could be relevant if the race develops into a tight finish, but the trainer T14 of 0/4 for Lucinda Russell & Michael Scudamore suggests the yard is not in its sharpest recent form.

races.name: Saints In The Community Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Noble Birth
runners_data.note: Front-runner by style at OR=120 and top weight of 168lbs for Clare Ellam; hasn't won in 5 recent runs and apprentice Maggs takes the ride, but if allowed to bowl along on Good ground his jumping accuracy will be the deciding factor — STYLE_FIT tag noted.|
runners_data.comment: Noble Birth is the one to beat on these figures, even without a win in his last five starts — a pair of fourths and a fifth show he's rarely far away. He has proven form over today's trip and going, though he was pulled up last time after a 79-day gap.

runners_data.name: Bold Light
runners_data.note: Lucinda Russell/Michael Scudamore's 9yo has only one comparable Good-ground run in the last 15 (0 wins, 0 places on that surface), making the going a mild concern, though he has placed at 2m and proximity to the pace suits the likely shape here.|
runners_data.comment: Bold Light is a leading danger, winless in his last five starts but rarely out of the frame with two thirds and two fourths in that sequence. He has proven form over today's trip and going, though an unseated run at the start of it and 59 days off are the concerns.

runners_data.name: Atlantic City
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy's 5yo shows outstanding form figures on Good ground (7/12 with one win and six places) and Sean Bowen is a top booking; back from 58 days off but has won fresh before — the trip of 2m4f is slightly longer than his best form but his class at OR=112 gives him a strong chance in this shape.|
runners_data.comment: Atlantic City is a leading danger, a winner two starts back, and runner-up last time out. The yard is in good form (29% last 14 days), she has proven form over today's trip and going, though 58 days off is on the longer side.

runners_data.name: Lets Mingle
runners_data.note: Listed as an unknown style and has unseated in recent form; Jack Power (5lb claim) helps the weight but the erratic profile makes this horse a wildcard — better in a truly run race that brings stamina into play over 2m4f on Good.|
runners_data.comment: Lets Mingle is a leading danger, winless in her last five starts but with two thirds in that sequence showing she is competitive. She has proven form over today's trip and going, though an unseated run three starts back, and a fifth last time out, are the risks from a 29-day break.

runners_data.name: Summergrounds
runners_data.note: Nicky Richards' 10yo was out just 16 days ago and ran third, keeping him race-fit; prominent style suits the expected shape and his Perth-grade handicap record (1W, 7P on soft-biased ground) suggests Good is actually his better surface.|
runners_data.comment: Summergrounds is a fair midfield yardstick: winless in his last five starts, though a pair of runner-up efforts earlier in that sequence show ability. A pulled-up run and a fifth are the concerns since. He has proven form over today's trip and going, back within just 16 days.

runners_data.name: Ceol Draiochta
runners_data.note: Young 5yo hold-up type for Adam Nicol with only Good-ground form on shorter trips (mostly 16f); stepping up significantly in distance to 2m4f is the key query, and Ryan Mania will need a strong pace to bring him into the race late.|
runners_data.comment: Ceol Draiochta is hard to fancy on these figures, winless in his last four starts with a fall and a pulled-up effort among them. He has run over today's going before, and his latest run, a fourth, is a rare sign of encouragement, though 49 days off adds a query.

runners_data.name: Pure Gold
runners_data.note: Lisa Harrison's 6yo has strong Good-ground experience (12/15 runs) and ran 10 days ago, so fitness is assured; in reality a front-running type who cannot find that berth here given the prominent traffic ahead — the redistribution to mid-pack means Callum Bewley must adapt his tactics and STYLE_FIT is rated at 0.90.|
runners_data.comment: Pure Gold is a fair midfield yardstick, winless in her last five starts with a fall among them, though back-to-back fourths in her last two starts show modest consistency. She has run over today's going before, and quickly returns to action within just 10 days.

runners_data.name: Parikarma
runners_data.note: Samuel Drinkwater's 9yo hold-up horse showed 2/24f/GOO last time, suggesting this trip on Good ground suits genuinely; amateur Imogen Mathias claims 7lbs which eases the OR=99 weight to a competitive level — best watched in a scenario where the pace is strong enough to bring him into contention.|
runners_data.comment: Parikarma is hard to fancy on these figures, winless in her last five starts, though a runner-up finish last time out is a shred of encouragement. Two thirds, a fifth and a below-par eighth make up the rest of that sequence. She has proven form over today's trip and going, from a 29-day break.

runners_data.name: Struth
runners_data.note: Russell/Scudamore's 6yo with tongue-tie and pull-through headgear has finished 5th, 6th, 6th in last three Good-ground runs (10/15 sim-going, 0W, 1P); Derek Fox is an experienced horseman but the form profile suggests this 9-year-old is below the level required to land this handicap.|
runners_data.comment: Struth is the outsider on these figures, winless in his last five starts and never inside the frame — twin sixths, twin fifths, and an unplaced effort. He has run over today's going before, but sits bottom of this field on our figures after a 35-day break.

races.paceDynamic: Noble Birth is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with several prominent-types in the field (Bold Light, Atlantic City, Summergrounds), will face some early pressure for position, though none are habitual tearaways at this trip. The pace is therefore likely to be honest but not breakneck — Good ground at Perth over 2m4f will keep things moving consistently without producing a true test of stamina. Pure Gold is a natural prominent racer who cannot secure that position given the volume of forward-going types ahead of him, and so effectively becomes a stalker rather than a pace-setter. This race shape — a clear leader pursued by a cluster of prominent horses on consistent Good ground — strongly favours those who can sit handy in second or third without burning reserves, meaning genuine prominent types with proven form at this track, trip and going will hold the structural advantage over hold-up runners who must wait for a gap that may never materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Noble Birth leads at a genuine but manageable clip and the prominent trio press without triggering a meltdown, the race becomes a test of jumping and class.
scenarios.body: Atlantic City's excellent Good-ground record (7/12 runners placed or better at similar going) and Sean Bowen's positional intelligence make him the ideal prominent stalker; Summergrounds' recent run 16 days ago and proven Perth-grade form mean he can sit second or third without wilting.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Pinged Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Noble Birth jumps boldly and the prominent challengers fail to assert, the leader controls fractions and the field strings out.
scenarios.body: Noble Birth's high STYLE_FIT as a natural front-runner means an uncontested lead from the off plays to his strengths, and a 9yo at OR=120 carrying 168lbs can conserve energy when unchallenged.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Finish Strong
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to exhaust the front rank and gaps open in the straight.
scenarios.body: Parikarma has solid Good-ground placed form over 2m4f (2/24f/GOO in last run) and amateur Imogen Mathias's 7lb claim softens the burden; Ceol Draiochta is a young 5yo who could benefit from a truly run race but has inconsistent form at this level.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Tactical Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If a slow early tempo turns the race into a messy sprint finish where positional luck determines the outcome.
scenarios.body: Lets Mingle's unpredictable style (U listed) and experience of tactical races at similar trips could produce a big run if the race falls apart; Pure Gold, pushed off his natural rhythm anyway, might stumble into a place in the chaos.

watchPoints.text: Atlantic City and Noble Birth — watch whether Bowen allows Noble Birth an uncontested lead or pushes Atlantic City forward immediately, as that early duel will set the pace tempo for the entire race.

Pure Gold — Callum Bewley cannot ride his horse's natural prominent race given the field's composition; watch for signs of frustration or a wide run if he can't find daylight through horses not in their natural positions.
Parikarma — Imogen Mathias (7lb claimer) is aboard a hold-up horse that needs a truly run race; if the pace is only honest rather than strong, the chance simply will not arrive in time.

Summergrounds — raced just 16 days ago; watch the paddock for any signs of a quick-return bounce, as a 10yo running at this frequency can sometimes present flat at the start even if handlers report well.

races.name: Sport, Education & Wellbeing Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Statuario
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen teams up with Mickey Bowen's runner, who is a genuine hold-up horse with strong credentials here — two wins on Good at 3m-plus trips in recent form and an excellent record across similar conditions (11/15 Good-going runs in the frame); 35 days since last run is fine, but he needs chaos ahead to get involved.
runners_data.comment: Statuario is the one to beat on these figures: two wins in his last five starts, one two starts back, with proven form over today's trip and going. The yard is in good form (27% last 14 days); an eighth in between is the only blot.

runners_data.name: Parisencore
runners_data.note: Nicky Richards stable is quiet at 0/2 in the last 14 days but Danny McMenamin rides, and this horse's entire chance rests on securing a soft, uncontested lead — its STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 is a reminder it is operating out of its comfort zone if pressured, but here the draw and lack of rivals means it likely gets away cleanly.
runners_data.comment: Parisencore rates a leading danger, runner-up last time out, with a win three starts back underlining his recent consistency. He has raced over today's going before and is fairly fresh at 21 days, though beaten in four of his last five he can still find one too good.

runners_data.name: Bleu D'enfer
runners_data.note: Donald McCain sends this horse 58 days fresh with tongue-tie applied; his best recent form has been at 20f on Good ground and the step up to 3m at Perth is a query, though his two placings at 20f Good suggest he handles conditions — he is a hold-up type who needs a strong pace to produce his best.
runners_data.comment: Bleu d'Enfer is a leading danger despite being winless in his last five starts, with two runner-up efforts including his latest outing. He has proven form over today's trip and going, though a below-par ninth two runs back is the risk after a 58-day break.

runners_data.name: Grand Clermont
runners_data.note: David Pipe's runner (1/6 in last 14 days) arrives just 14 days between runs and is fitted with tongue-tie; he has two wins at 24f on Good and looked progressive when second at 23f recently — tracking the pace prominently with Rian Corcoran claiming 5lb makes this a legitimate each-way player if the front runs.
runners_data.comment: Grand Clermont is a leading danger with two wins in his last five starts, one of them three starts back, and he's already proven over today's trip and going. Quick to return after just 14 days, with a below-par sixth his only blip in that sequence.

runners_data.name: Walk On Quest
runners_data.note: Lucinda Russell and Michael Scudamore's runner goes in tongue-tie and won over 24f Good just two runs ago then followed up with a placing — Derek Fox takes the ride and this seven-year-old's age and recent form makes him one of the more dangerous prominent types if Parisencore is caught.
runners_data.comment: Walk On Quest is a fair yardstick for the middle order: a win two starts back shows he retains ability, but a below-par eighth followed last time out. He has proven form over today's trip and going, with a 35-day break that could bring him on again.

runners_data.name: Wasdell Dundalk
runners_data.note: Lowest rated runner in the field at OR 112 and 10 days between runs for Lisa Harrison's yard (0/1 past 14 days); a genuine hold-up horse in reality whose position on the map understates how far back it will sit — without a strong gallop to aim at, finding the winner from this type of role at Perth over 3m looks a stiff ask.
runners_data.comment: Wasdell Dundalk is hard to fancy on these figures, winless in his last five starts, though his latest run was a modest runner-up finish. He has proven form over today's trip and going, but the wider form line, no better than fourth before that, keeps him among the outsiders.

runners_data.name: Inis Oirr
runners_data.note: Two consecutive second-place finishes including a recent win over 24f Good gives Inis Oirr solid claims on form; a true hold-up horse in practice despite its map position — Patrick Wadge rides and the headgear flag (p, presumably) could sharpen its jumping, but it needs the race run honestly to deliver its finishing effort.
runners_data.comment: Inis Oirr is an outsider on these figures but shows scattered ability - a ninth four starts back, then a win three starts back, and back-to-back runner-up efforts in his last two starts. He has proven form over today's trip and going, but the overall profile rates modest for this field.

races.paceDynamic: Parisencore is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pressing rival likely to challenge for the lead, Danny McMenamin can control tempo from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop over this 3m Perth test on Good ground. Grand Clermont and Walk On Quest will push forward to track the leader, creating a compact prominent group across the early stages, but neither is likely to apply aggressive pressure that forces Parisencore to race at a punishing clip. Statuario, Bleu D'enfer, Wasdell Dundalk and Inis Oirr sit rearward — though Wasdell Dundalk and Inis Oirr are genuine hold-up horses who have been mapped to midfield because the rear is overcrowded with closers, meaning their natural deepest position is unlikely to materialise. The race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or capable of tracking the pace, since a controlled front-running tempo at Perth typically keeps enough petrol in the tank for the leader and chasers to repel late challengers who must cover extra ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Parisencore Controls, Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Parisencore is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets a measured pace that suits a strong traveller throughout.
scenarios.body: McMenamin dictates every yard from the front on Good ground at Perth, rating the race perfectly and having enough in reserve at the final fence to kick again; this is the dominant shape given there is zero confirmed rival to test his position from the outset.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chasers Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely sustainable but Parisencore flattens out late, handing the race to one of the tracking prominent types.
scenarios.body: Grand Clermont or Walk On Quest, sitting just off the pace throughout, simply stay on strongest when Parisencore finds nothing extra after the last; both have sound Good-ground form at this trip and Rian Corcoran's 5lb claim helps Grand Clermont's cause on a flat-ish finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is stronger than anticipated and Parisencore burns rivals off, leaving a late-finishing gap that a genuine closer can exploit.
scenarios.body: Statuario, the most authentic hold-up horse in the field with Sean Bowen aboard and proven Good-ground winning form at 3m trips, is best placed to benefit from any late attrition through the field; Bleu D'enfer, tongue-tied here, also stays well enough to pick up pieces.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Pace Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If Parisencore jumps poorly or is taken off its feet early, causing the entire race shape to break down unpredictably.
scenarios.body: With the field then bunched and no obvious leader, a horse who can travel fluidly mid-pack and quicken relative to rivals — Grand Clermont or Walk On Quest — holds the tactical edge to capitalise on any reshuffling.

watchPoints.text: Parisencore's jumping is pivotal — if McMenamin meets a fence wrong early and the horse loses its lead position it is racing out of role and its chance evaporates rapidly.

Grand Clermont ran just 14 days ago and carries tongue-tie; if Rian Corcoran finds the horse below par from a quick return, the second-most prominent position in this race is vacated and the shape changes significantly.

Wasdell Dundalk and Inis Oirr — both genuine hold-up horses likely sitting deeper than their map position — will need a genuinely strong pace to close late; if the gallop is modest, watch for both to be outpaced before they can produce their effort.

Perth's 3m trip returns Good ground all day per the going report — no horse faces a meaningful surface concern, meaning fitness, jumping fluency and tactical positioning are the primary differentiators rather than conditions.

Statuario's 11-year-old age combined with Sean Bowen's hold-up ride from a big weight (169lbs) means any jumping error from a tired rival in the final half-mile could hand him a run of daylight he needs — watch his challenge from the second-last fence.

races.name: Saints Kidz Community Football Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Ballintubber Boy
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with a consistent recent record including two second-place finishes in similar Good-ground conditions; Toby McCain-Mitchell (3) takes 3lb off, which matters at these weights, and his sim-going record of 12/15 makes the surface no concern over a trip he handles well.
runners_data.comment: Ballintubber Boy earns our vote on profile: a strong middle sequence of two runner-up efforts and a third, albeit winless, though his last two starts dipped to sixth and fourth. He has proven form over today's trip and going and returns fresh after a 31-day break.

runners_data.name: Secret Trix
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen in the saddle is a significant booking for Olly Murphy's hold-up performer, who has been placed in five of his last five starts on Good or similar ground; the 3m trip looks within range but he's yet to win beyond 2m4f, and his natural late style may be compromised if Speed Davis crawls.
runners_data.comment: Secret Trix rates the leading danger having gone close in four of his last five starts, twice runner-up including his latest, without managing to get his head in front. He has proven form over today's trip and going, though a seventh earlier in that sequence and 38 days off are considerations.

runners_data.name: Speed Davis
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's runner holds a confirmed front-running berth and is the one horse assured of getting his natural position; his STYLE_FIT tag of 0.93 acknowledges that in other race shapes he would be racing out of role, but in this context he is the architect — his stamina over 3m on Good is the key question, with a mixed sim-going record of 8/15.
runners_data.comment: Speed Davis is a leading danger on the back of consecutive wins two and three starts back. He has proven form over today's trip and going, though a fifth last time out and a sixth before that pair show he needs things to fall right for him.

runners_data.name: Spit Spot
runners_data.note: Lucinda Russell and Michael Scudamore's prominent racer has 81 days since his last completed run (flagged as a fitness query) and his recent form includes a pull-up; the headgear note (tp) and his record of 1W4P on Good ground suggest ability, but fitness after that layoff and an interrupted campaign are genuine concerns.
runners_data.comment: Spit Spot is a leading danger on the strength of a win five starts back, and she has proven form over today's trip and going. That success is the outlier though: a pulled-up effort last time out, plus a seventh, fourth and sixth in between, are the risk.

runners_data.name: Lowlands
runners_data.note: Nicky Richards' runner is by nature a hold-up performer, but the density of closers in this field means he is mapped to midfield rather than his preferred rearward berth; his form figures of 223-12 are sharp and his Good-ground record is solid, though the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) signals he may not get the race run to suit him here.
runners_data.comment: Lowlands offers a balanced case for the middle order, a winner two starts back, with three runner-up efforts elsewhere in her recent form, but she has not added a second success since. She has run over today's going before, and the 46-day gap since her last run is on the longer side.

runners_data.name: Ebselysees
runners_data.note: Susan Corbett's runner has won twice in fourteen starts on Good or similar ground and carries the lowest weight in the field at 150lbs; a genuine closer by inclination, he is pushed forward on the map because the field is rear-heavy — the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) means the scenario that delivers his best chance requires a pace he may not get.
runners_data.comment: Ebselysees is hard to fancy on these figures despite a pair of wins two and three starts back, with her form either side of that at seventh and fifth, last time out, well below that level. She has proven form over today's trip and going, from a 36-day break.

runners_data.name: Dalileo
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes takes over on Lisa Harrison's 11-year-old, who returns just 10 days after his last run having won at 3m on Good — that recent course-and-distance form is notable; his prominent style suits this race shape well and his sim-going record of 12/15 underlines the surface is no barrier, though age and quick turnaround are worth monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Dalileo is the outsider on these figures but arrives fresh off a win last time out, just 10 days ago — his only success in these last five starts, with a seventh and fourth among the finishes before it. He has proven form over today's trip and going.

races.paceDynamic: Speed Davis is the lone confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, without a natural challenger pressing him, is set to control proceedings from the front at a sustainable gallop over 3m on Good ground at Perth. Spit Spot and Dalileo add prominent-racing weight to the early sections, meaning Speed Davis will not be entirely unchallenged, but neither is a pure front-runner likely to seriously disrupt his rhythm. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Lowlands and Ebselysees are genuine closers by preference but are shown in midfield positions because the pace map cannot place all of them at the back where they would naturally settle. A controlled, single-pace gallop set by Speed Davis over an extended trip on Good turf strongly favours horses who travel prominently and have the stamina to sustain their effort — prominent-to-midfield profiles with proven 3m ability are best placed, while true closers dependent on a strong pace to generate late momentum face an unfavourable race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Speed Davis Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Speed Davis is allowed to bowl along in front at his own tempo with no serious challenger disputing the lead.
scenarios.body: Speed Davis sets a measured, controlled gallop and the field strings out behind him with no one willing or able to pressure him; horses who travel fluently in his slipstream and stay the trip on Good ground are best positioned to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pressurise
scenarios.trigger: If Spit Spot or Dalileo push forward aggressively to test Speed Davis from an early stage, raising the tempo.
scenarios.body: A more genuinely run race over 3m on Good ground stretches the field and makes stamina the decisive factor; horses who can travel prominently but have proven staying power will outlast those who find the early pace too hot.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners set enough of a gallop to leave them vulnerable in the closing stages over this stiff 3m trip.
scenarios.body: Horses who have been held up or settled in midfield can close ground as the leaders tire from the final hurdle home; however, this scenario is undermined because Lowlands and Ebselysees — the most natural closers — are mapped out of their true roles and may not secure genuinely deep positions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors, fallers or a stop-start pace cause the field to bunch and fragment unpredictably across the 3m trip.
scenarios.body: With older, handicapped hurdlers over a stamina-testing trip, attrition can play a role; horses with clean jumping records and adaptable tactical profiles survive best when the race shape breaks down.

watchPoints.text: Speed Davis — if he is allowed to hack along unchallenged on the front end, the race may effectively be decided by how well he jumps the final two hurdles; any jumping error at pace could reshuffle the entire finish.
Spit Spot — his 81-day absence combined with a pull-up last time out means fitness is unproven; watch his jumping and movement in the early stages as a guide to whether he is fully wound up.

Lowlands and Ebselysees — both are natural closers mapped out of their true roles; if neither settles as deep as they would prefer, their finishing kicks may be blunted and their chance materially reduced.

Dalileo — returning on just a 10-day turnaround having won last time, Brian Hughes will need to manage him carefully in the early stages over 3m; if he travels too keenly tracking Speed Davis, stamina could become a question late.

races.name: Scone Palace International Horse Trials Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Centurion's Sister
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner who should enjoy a lead she is rarely afforded; trainer Nicky Richards in decent form (1 from 4 in 14 days) and 16-day turnaround is sharp enough, but sim-going record of 0 wins from 4 places suggests she tends to find one too good when it matters.
runners_data.comment: Ultra-consistent without a win — second last time, and placed in all of her last five starts (three seconds and two thirds). A 16-day break keeps her fresh, and she has form over today's distance and going — the pick on profile at 101 with us.

runners_data.name: Scots Poet
runners_data.note: Three wins and six places from 15 similar-going starts is outstanding course-and-conditions evidence; Ewan Whillans' yard freshened him up over 35 days, and back at the 2m trip where he has won twice on Good, he is the textbook prominent racer this shape should suit.
runners_data.comment: A revitalised sort — won his last two starts and three of his last five (1-1-2-1-3). It's 35 days since that latest success, and we rate him just 95, below his official mark of 99, despite proven form over today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Follow Charlie
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and comes from a trainer with zero wins from 13 runners in the past fortnight; his hold-up style is his natural register, though the 59-day break and step back from longer distances are the key things to monitor before he can be fully trusted here.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts, including a below-form ninth, but he tops our figures at 103, well clear of his 98 official mark. Fitness the query after 59 days off, though he holds form over today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Jolyjump
runners_data.note: 378 days off the track is the critical fact; the Gary & Josh Moore yard has been active (4 from 26 in 14 days) but this much time away from competition introduces significant unknown risk, and his genuine hold-up style needs pace to aim at which this shape may not reliably provide.
runners_data.comment: Big absentee back after 378 days off, but there's solid recent form — two runner-ups before a below-par eighth last time. Yet to win in his last four, rated 98 with us, in line with his 97 official mark, and form over today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Tigress Lilly
runners_data.note: Recent form of 700-66 on Good ground at this trip is simply not compelling; her natural style is rear-of-field but the compressed field means she will be ridden closer than ideal, and the STYLE_FIT flag legitimately tempers expectations that she can reproduce anything better than mid-division finishes.
runners_data.comment: Hard to fancy — well held in each of her last five starts, including two unplaced efforts, and yet to win in that run. Fresh 10 days after her latest outing and with form over today's distance and going, but rated below her 92 official mark.

runners_data.name: Storm The Dug
runners_data.note: Showed ability when second at 2m on Good ground two runs back, and the Lucinda Russell & Michael Scudamore yard has placed him again quickly (35 days); a true hold-up horse forced towards midfield in this shape, his best chance requires a stronger pace than Centurion's Sister alone is likely to generate.
runners_data.comment: A workmanlike sort, yet to win in his last five, though he ran a good second two starts back, alongside a below-form ninth earlier in the sequence. Rated above his 92 official mark with form over today's distance and going, but a fifth last time keeps questions open.

runners_data.name: Malangen
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old making his second start in 10 days for a small operation (0 from 1 in 14 days); his sim-going record of 0 wins from 11 similar-going attempts is a notable flag, though he has the prominent style to sit close and could make the frame if the pace is misjudged.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last six starts, which include an unseated-rider effort and a well-beaten eighth last time, leaving him bottom of our figures. There's some encouragement though — three runner-up efforts in that run, fresh 10 days ago, with form over today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Lucky In Taipan
runners_data.note: 300 days off the track is an enormous question mark for a four-year-old with form figures of 7P60 in his best visible runs; naturally a hold-up horse shuffled toward midfield on the map, this return from a long absence for Fergal O'Brien makes him very hard to trust in any scenario.
runners_data.comment: Big field of intrigue for this one — unraced for 300 days and yet to win in his last four, including a pulled-up effort. Yet we rate him a stunning 101, way above his 74 official mark, and he does hold form over today's distance and going.

races.paceDynamic: Centurion's Sister is the lone confirmed front-runner here and should stride into an uncontested lead from the outset on Good ground over 2m at Perth, with Scots Poet and Malangen likely to press from prominent positions just behind. With only one horse genuinely drawn to lead, the pace will be controlled and sustainable rather than searching, creating a race run at an honest but not punishing tempo — conditions that typically favour those able to track the leader closely and pounce approaching the final flight. The field contains more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the rear; Tigress Lilly, Storm The Dug, and Lucky In Taipan are all genuine hold-up horses that the map has redistributed into midfield positions because natural room at the back is compressed, meaning their true closing threat may be blunted by the positions they are forced to adopt. The shape firmly favours prominent racers who can travel within range of Centurion's Sister throughout, avoiding the inevitable shuffle-back that awaits the redistibuted hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Centurion's Sister sets a steady, uncontested pace and the prominent chasers track smoothly throughout.
scenarios.body: Centurion's Sister dictates from the front with Scots Poet sitting a length or two off the pace, and the lack of pressure means the leader or the closest pursuer has plenty left to give from two out; this shape rewards horses that race prominently without burning unnecessary energy.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Outsprinted Late
scenarios.trigger: If the controlled early pace leaves enough in the tank for a midfield horse to accelerate sharply from two out.
scenarios.body: Jolyjump or Follow Charlie, tracking just off the pace in midfield, finds a clear run off the final turn and picks off the front two who have been sparring all the way; the Good ground allows the late kick to function on a course where staying power meets a sharp enough test.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistibuted Closers Fire
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops with enough early zip that the front two tire, allowing the true hold-up horses to outfinish them despite imperfect positions.
scenarios.body: Storm The Dug or Tigress Lilly, unable to settle as far back as natural, still finds themselves closer than usual and benefits from a rare strong pace; however, this scenario is discounted because these horses are unlikely to achieve their optimal hold-up position and their recent form offers limited encouragement.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Blunts Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Centurion's Sister is pressed unexpectedly by Malangen or another into an unsustainable early tempo and weakens from the final fence.
scenarios.body: A rare contested pace would open the race up entirely, gifting a fresher, well-positioned horse an unlikely opportunity; Scots Poet, with superior recent form and multiple wins on Good ground, is best placed to capitalise even in a scramble.

watchPoints.text: Scots Poet's sim-going record (3W/6P from 15 attempts on Good) is significantly stronger than any other runner's — watch whether Charlie Maggs slots him directly behind Centurion's Sister from the off, as that is the position that wins this race shape.

Centurion's Sister has never won from this prominent position across four similar-going runs — if she shows any sign of idling or shortening stride approaching the last, the horses immediately behind will swamp her quickly.

Jolyjump's 378-day absence is the biggest single risk variable in the race; watch whether he jumps fluently and travels with any enthusiasm in the early stages, as a laboured round of jumping from a horse this rusty could compromise any horse immediately behind him.

Storm The Dug and Tigress Lilly are both trained by Lucinda Russell & Michael Scudamore and share a natural hold-up style — if either is ridden aggressively to secure a better position than expected, they could disrupt the prominent runners' rhythm in the first half mile.

Lucky In Taipan (300 days off, form figures unremarkable) is the most likely finisher to be eased or pulled up if not travelling — his position on the track in the middle stages is worth tracking to avoid any interference for the market principles.
